name: oxipng-animation-reduction
instr:
Oxipng currently disables reductions for APNGs. Please add an opt-in mode that reduces a retained animation as one unit, so a smaller pixel format doesn't corrupt later frames. Add the public field `oxipng::Options::apng_reductions: bool`, defaulting to `false`, and make it work through the existing optimization entry points.

When enabled, choose a shared format from the default image and every animation frame, including the default image when it isn't part of the animation. Apply these structural reductions whenever their existing option switches allow them, rather than choosing them by compressed size: lossless 16-to-8 sample reduction, RGB-to-grayscale conversion, removal of fully opaque alpha channels, compaction of an indexed palette by removing unused entries and merging identical RGBA entries, and the lowest lossless grayscale or indexed bit depth. Grayscale conversion requires both `color_type_reduction` and `grayscale_reduction`; alpha removal requires `color_type_reduction`. Do not introduce indexed/channel conversions or alpha-to-transparency-key conversion in this mode. Palette ordering is up to you.

The resulting PNG must retain the animation's pixels and frame controls, with every image encoded in the shared format and the interlacing requested by `Options::interlace`. A structural change must rewrite affected compressed data even when `idat_recoding` is false. Follow the existing chunk cleanup and explicit `StripChunks::Keep` protection policies unless metada
